hero.subtitulo: A journey of faith, prayer and reparation in the heart of Portugal, under the mantle of the Mother of God.

sobre.intro: The pilgrimage of Our Lady of Christendom – Portugal is an annual pilgrimage to the Shrine of Fátima, organised by a group of lay Catholics devoted to the Traditional Holy Mass. It takes place around 12 October, the eve of the anniversary of Our Lady's last apparition at Fátima (the Miracle of the Sun).
sobre.missao_p1: This pilgrimage was born from a profound desire to make known, or rediscover, the Holy Tradition of the Church in Portugal. Our country was once a central instrument in the hands of Our Lady for the evangelisation of the world. Our great goal is that Portugal may once more assume that role in the service of Our Lady and the Holy Church.
sobre.missao_p2: Our Lady, at Fátima, promised that in Portugal <it>«the dogma of the faith will always be preserved.»</it> That promise was not given so that we may rest comfortably, but precisely so that we commit ourselves ever more to evangelisation, offering prayers, sacrifices and mortifications for our Homeland and for the Holy Father.
sobre.fe_texto: Walking in the footsteps of the saints who preceded us, praying the Holy Rosary and assisting at Holy Mass in the traditional rite.
sobre.tradicao_texto: Rediscovering the liturgical and spiritual richness of the Portuguese Catholic heritage, in communion with the Church of all ages.
sobre.cristandade_texto: Publicly reaffirming the Christian faith and the desire to restore all things in Christ, under the protection of Mary.

historia.e1983_texto: In 1983, a group of young French Catholics began a pilgrimage from Paris to Chartres in the spirit of apostolic tradition. What began as a small gesture became, decades later, the largest youth pilgrimage in Europe.
historia.e2010_titulo: Nuestra Señora de la Cristiandad — Luján
historia.e2010_texto: In 2010, the Nuestra Señora de la Cristiandad pilgrimage was born in Argentina, journeying to the celebrated Shrine of Luján. Gathering faithful devoted to the liturgical Tradition, it extends the movement to the American continent.
historia.e2021_titulo: Nuestra Señora de la Cristiandad — Covadonga
historia.e2021_texto: In 2021, a pilgrimage of Nuestra Señora de la Cristiandad was established in Spain, heading to the historic Shrine of Covadonga in Asturias — cradle of the Christian Reconquista and symbol of Iberian faith.
historia.e2025_texto: Inspired by the French example and the growing thirst for tradition among young Portuguese Catholics, the vision of a similar pilgrimage on Portuguese soil is born, under the patronage of Our Lady.
historia.e2026_titulo: Pilgrimage of Our Lady of Christendom
historia.e2026_texto: With the support of laypeople and priests devoted to the liturgical tradition, the second Portuguese edition of the pilgrimage takes place, gathering faithful of all ages.
historia.e2026b_texto: In 2026, a new pilgrimage is born from Rome to Subiaco, following the paths of Saint Benedict — father of Western monasticism — from the Eternal City to the cave where the Saint lived in penance and from which Benedictine spirituality sprang.
historia.nazare_descricao: From the miracle of D. Fuas Roupinho to the ancient image brought by the Visigoths — the history of the shrine where the pilgrimage begins.
historia.missa_descricao: The Traditional Roman Rite, Gregorian chant and the Holy Rosary as the spiritual structure of each day of walking.
historia.fatima_descricao: The 1917 apparitions, Our Lady's promise for Portugal and the meaning of arriving at the Cova da Iria on the eve of the Miracle of the Sun.

percurso.subtitulo: An itinerary through the shrines and monuments of the heart of Portugal, punctuated by daily Masses, the Rosary and Gregorian chants.

rota.subtitulo: Three days on foot through the shrines and monuments of central Portugal, following in the footsteps of medieval pilgrims.

faq.q1: Where do we sleep along the route?
faq.a1_resto: The organisation provides overnight accommodation in gymnasiums or sports halls along the route.
faq.a2_antes: Gradual physical preparation and good prior hydration.
faq.a2_durante: Maintain silence and a spirit of prayer; obey the column leaders.
faq.q3: What footwear and sleeping equipment should I bring?
a3_sapatos_items: Comfortable and sturdy footwear (do not bring new trainers)
Optional: moisturising cream, petroleum jelly, etc.
faq.q4: What to pack in the small backpack (for walking)?
faq.a4_intro: This backpack accompanies you throughout the entire walk.
a4_items: Medication for headaches or muscle pain
faq.q5: What to pack in the large backpack (transported by the organisation)?
faq.a5_intro: This backpack is transported by the organisation from one camp to the next — you do not carry it during the walk.
a5_items: Personal hygiene items, towel and swimsuit
First aid supplies (nurses will only attend to serious cases)
faq.q6: Who can take part in the pilgrimage?
faq.a6: The pilgrimage is open to all Catholic faithful aged 14 and over. Those under 18 must be accompanied by a responsible adult or present written authorisation from their guardians.
faq.a7: Some prior training is recommended, as the route involves walking an average of 20 km per day. However, a support group and transport will be available for pilgrims with occasional difficulties.
faq.q9: Which liturgical rite will be celebrated?
faq.a9: All Holy Masses will be celebrated in the Traditional Roman Rite (Tridentine Mass), with Gregorian chant.
faq.q11: How can I support the pilgrimage without taking part?
faq.a11: You can support through donations, by spreading the word, or by offering prayers for the pilgrims. Contact us about volunteering and logistical support.

nazare.meta_title: Nazaré — Pilgrimage of Our Lady of Christendom
nazare.meta_desc: The history, legend and devotion of the Shrine of Our Lady of Nazaré, the starting point of the pilgrimage.
nazare.subtitulo: High on the promontory of the Sítio da Nazaré stands one of the oldest and most venerated Marian shrines in Portugal — a centre of devotion deeply connected to the sea and the life of the local people.
nazare.intro: High on the promontory of the Sítio da Nazaré, facing the vast Atlantic, stands one of the oldest and most venerated Marian shrines in Portugal: the Shrine of Our Lady of Nazaré. Its history interweaves tradition, faith and miracles, being a centre of devotion deeply connected to the sea and the life of the local people.
nazare.s1_titulo: The Legend and Miracle of D. Fuas Roupinho
nazare.s1_p1: Tradition recounts that on the morning of 14 September 1182, the feast of the Exaltation of the Holy Cross, the governor of Porto de Mós, D. Fuas Roupinho, was riding through fog near the cliff of the Sítio when he spotted a deer and gave chase. Without realising, he approached dangerously close to the precipice. At that moment, he fervently invoked the Virgin Mary, whose small image was venerated in the region. Miraculously, the horse halted at the very edge of the abyss, saving the rider's life.
nazare.s1_p2: In gratitude, D. Fuas ordered a small chapel to be built on the spot, over the grotto where the image of the Virgin with the Child was kept, known as «Our Lady of Nazaré». To this day, next to the ancient chapel, the legendary hoofprint carved in the rock is preserved, a testimony to the devotion and memory of the miracle.
nazare.s2_titulo: The Image and Its Ancient Origin
nazare.s2_p1: The devotion to Our Lady of Nazaré centres on a small and very ancient wooden image, of simple but deeply symbolic features. Christian tradition relates that the sculpture represents the Virgin Mary nursing the Child Jesus — which is why it is known as the «Virgin of the Milk». According to pious tradition, the image was originally carved by Saint Joseph during Jesus's childhood, and later painted by the evangelist Saint Luke.
nazare.s2_p2: In the early centuries of Christianity, the image remained in the Holy Land, later taken to a monastery in Palestine. In the 4th century, during the iconoclast persecutions and the threat of destruction of sacred icons, the monk Cyriacus transported the image to North Africa, entrusting it to Saint Jerome and later to Saint Augustine, Bishop of Hippo. From there it passed to the monastery of Cauliniana, near Mérida, in Spain.
nazare.s2_p3: With the Muslim invasion of the Iberian Peninsula in the early 8th century, the image was hidden to protect it. The last Visigoth king, D. Rodrigo, defeated at the Battle of Guadalete (711), fled accompanied by a monk named Frei Romano. Together they brought the image and concealed it in a small grotto, by the sea, high on a promontory — what we know today as the Sítio da Nazaré. There it remained hidden and forgotten for several centuries until it was rediscovered in the time of D. Fuas, giving rise to popular devotion.
nazare.s3_p1: The small chapel built by D. Fuas quickly became a place of pilgrimage. Devotion grew so much that, already in the 14th century, during the reign of D. Fernando I, a first larger temple was built, which would become the nucleus of the present Shrine.
nazare.s3_p2: In the 17th century, the building was profoundly remodelled and enlarged, acquiring the layout we know today, with its beautiful baroque façade and two bell towers. Inside, the altarpiece of the high altar stands out, where the ancient image of Our Lady of Nazaré continues to be venerated with great piety.
nazare.s3_p3: For centuries, the Shrine of Our Lady of Nazaré was one of the principal Marian devotions of central Portugal, attracting pilgrims from all regions of the country and even from abroad.
nazare.s3_p4: Numerous miracles are attributed to the intercession of the Virgin of Nazaré, especially among seafaring folk who led an arduous and dangerous life. The entrance to the bar of Nazaré was (and remains) perilous, with violent waves and treacherous currents. When shipwrecks occurred or danger threatened at sea, the fishermen's wives would climb the promontory of the Sítio and fervently pray for the protection of their loved ones, often on their knees or prostrate before the image.

missa.meta_title: The Holy Mass — Pilgrimage of Our Lady of Christendom
missa.meta_desc: The traditional Roman rite, Gregorian chant and the central role of the Holy Mass in the spirituality of the pilgrimage.
missa.subtitulo: The entire journey is oriented towards the Sacrifice of the Altar. The Holy Mass in the Traditional Roman Rite is the source and summit of each day of pilgrimage.
missa.intro: The Holy Mass is the unbloody renewal of the Sacrifice of Our Lord Jesus Christ on Calvary, and constitutes the centre of all Catholic spirituality and the most perfect expression of the doctrine of the Holy Church. In the Holy Mass its four principal ends are accomplished in a sublime manner:
missa.fim1_desc: To render God the worship He Himself desires to receive.
missa.fim2_desc: To give praise for the innumerable gifts and benefits we have received from Him.
missa.fim3_desc: To offer satisfaction for our sins and those of the whole world.
missa.fim4_desc: To humbly ask for the graces necessary for our salvation.
missa.p2: The pilgrimage is not a sporting march nor a mere cultural journey. It is an act of worship. Its heart is the Holy Mass celebrated in the Traditional Roman Rite — the same rite that shaped the spirituality of Christendom for over a thousand years.
missa.s1_p1: All Masses of the pilgrimage are celebrated according to the Traditional Roman Rite, commonly known as the Tridentine Mass or the Mass of All Ages. In this rite, the priest celebrates ad orientem — facing the East, that is, symbolically oriented towards God — in an attitude of adoration, united with the faithful.
missa.s1_p2: The Mass is celebrated in Latin, the sacred and universal language of the Church, which transcends cultural barriers and unites pilgrims of diverse origins in a single prayer. By pilgrimming and participating in these Masses, the faithful enters a living tradition that unites him with the martyrs, the saints and the faithful of all ages.
missa.s2_p1: Gregorian chant holds a central place in the pilgrimage. Recognised by the Church as the proper chant of the Roman liturgy, it elevates the soul and disposes the heart to prayer. Throughout the route, pilgrims sing chants in Latin and in Portuguese, creating an atmosphere of recollection and continual prayer.
missa.s3_p1: The meditated Rosary accompanies the moments of silence during the walk, transforming the route into a true school of prayer and contemplation, which goes far beyond mere physical effort.
missa.s3_p2: United with Our Lady, we walk with our foremost spiritual weapon, in the battle that leads us to Heaven.
missa.s4_p1: The pilgrimage begins with the Opening Mass, celebrated at the Shrine of Nazaré — a solemn Mass of blessing and consecration of the pilgrims to the Immaculate Heart of Mary, in which Her protection and intercession for the days ahead is invoked.
missa.s4_p2: The route culminates with the Closing Mass, in Fátima, celebrated in thanksgiving for the gift of the pilgrimage and in reparation for the sins of Christendom. It is the moment in which the outward journey unites with the inward journey, and in which the pilgrim renews his consecration to Our Lady.

fatima.meta_title: Fátima — Pilgrimage of Our Lady of Christendom
fatima.meta_desc: The 1917 apparitions, Our Lady's message and the devotion to the Immaculate Heart of Mary in Portugal.
fatima.subtitulo: The Shrine of Fátima was born in the heart of Portugal from a series of supernatural events that profoundly marked the Church in the 20th century.
fatima.intro: One year before Our Lady's visits, Lucia dos Santos and her cousins Francisco and Jacinta Marto, three humble shepherds from Aljustrel, received three visits from the Angel of Portugal, also called the Angel of Peace. He taught them prayers of adoration, penance and reparation, preparing them for the great mission God had entrusted to them. During the visits, the Angel invited them to offer sacrifices and to pray especially «for sinners and for peace in the world».
fatima.ap1_texto: Our Lady presented herself as «coming from Heaven» and asked the children to pray the Rosary every day to bring about peace and the end of the war. She promised them: «You will suffer greatly, but the grace of God will be your comfort.» She also announced that Francisco and Jacinta would soon go to Heaven, while Lucia would remain longer to make known the devotion to the Immaculate Heart of Mary.
fatima.ap2_texto: The Virgin revealed God's desire to establish in the world devotion to Her Immaculate Heart. The crowd surrounded the apparitions, asking for reparation. Lucia received the grace of understanding that her mission would be to spread this devotion, while Francisco and Jacinta would be taken early to Heaven.
fatima.ap3_texto: Our Lady revealed the famous Secret of Fátima in three parts. The children saw a vision of hell; the necessity of devotion to the Immaculate Heart as a means of salvation and conversion was announced to them; and a prophecy about the future sufferings of the Church, the Pope and the world. Our Lady promised: «In the end, my Immaculate Heart will triumph.»
fatima.ap4_texto: As the children had been detained on the 13th, the Virgin appeared to them later, at Valinhos, reaffirming the request for sacrifices and prayers for sinners and promising a miracle in October, «so that all may believe».
fatima.ap5_texto: Before a crowd of about 30,000 people, Our Lady returned and insisted on the Rosary and sacrifices. Many pilgrims witnessed signs, such as the fall of white petals that disappeared before touching the ground, and a luminous cloud over the holm oak.
fatima.ap6_texto: The last apparition was witnessed by a crowd of 50,000 to 70,000 people, including sceptics and journalists. Our Lady identified herself as «Our Lady of the Rosary» and again asked for the daily recitation of the Rosary and conversion. That day the Miracle of the Sun occurred: the sun appeared to detach itself from the sky, spinning and casting coloured lights, before «dancing» and plunging towards the crowd. The phenomenon, witnessed by thousands, confirmed to the eyes of the world the truth of the apparitions. Francisco and Jacinta died shortly afterwards, victims of the pneumonic influenza epidemic, offering their sufferings «for sinners». Lucia, who would live until 2005, became the principal messenger of devotion to the Immaculate Heart of Mary.
fatima.pp1_texto: Lucia saw the Virgin and the Child Jesus, who asked her for the reparatory devotion of the five First Saturdays in honour of the Immaculate Heart. Our Lady promised: «To all those who practise it, I promise to assist them at the hour of death with all the graces necessary for salvation.»
fatima.pp2_texto: The Child Jesus reappeared, confirming the importance of the reparatory devotion and clarifying that confession could be made a few days before or after, provided there was the intention to make reparation to the Heart of Mary.
fatima.pp3_texto: Lucia had a sublime vision of the mystery of the Most Holy Trinity. Our Lady then explicitly requested the consecration of Russia to Her Immaculate Heart by the Pope, in union with all the bishops. She later lamented that this request had not been heeded in time, warning of the consequences: the spread of the errors of atheism, persecutions of the Church and suffering of the Holy Father.
fatima.devocao_titulo: Devotion to the Immaculate Heart of Mary in Portugal
fatima.devocao_p1: Portugal has a particularly rich history of devotion to the Immaculate Heart of Mary, expressed in the lives of several contemporary mystics: the Venerable Sister Lucia, Blessed Alexandrina Maria da Costa and Mother Virgínia Brites da Paixão.
fatima.devocao_p2: Blessed Alexandrina stood out in an extraordinary way: for years she mystically relived the Passion of Christ every Friday from 1 pm to 3 pm, and lived for 13 years sustained only by Holy Communion, a fact verified by medical examinations. She had mystical experiences similar to those of Lucia, with apparitions of Jesus and Mary, and even of angels who brought her Communion when a priest could not do so. It was through her influence that Pope Pius XII performed the first consecration of the world to the Immaculate Heart of Mary.
